reasons: Reads as two necklaces (rule 2). The chain forms two separate loops on the vase. An inner short loop carries the toggle (clasp at x≈960-1110, y≈1380-1555, ~7 cm below the neck). There the strands overlap into one column, and nothing in frame shows they are one chain. At a glance this is a layered look: a toggle choker plus a second plain paperclip chain. The product is a single 50 cm strand.
notes: The link count supports one chain doubled. About 14 links show in the inner loop's front, ~26 in the outer loop's front, and ~12 are hidden behind the ~3.7 cm wrap. That is ~52 links at ~9.9 mm pitch, about 51 cm. As two separate necklaces they would be ~22 cm and ~32 cm, neither of them the product. So 'one chain wrapped twice' is the only length-consistent reading. But a 50 cm chain cannot be doubled on a human neck, so even that reading misleads under 'Made for every neck'. The brief asked for one loop.

fix: Keep the vase, tulip, ledge, light and framing. Re-shoot with the chain once around the neck: 'one single strand goes once around the vase's neck; both sides fall over the shoulders and meet in ONE long loop resting on the belly, the closed toggle at the front centre; only one strand of chain anywhere in frame, never doubled, never wrapped twice, never layered.'
